options.content:
Cloudflare allows **1200 API requests per 5 minutes per token**, and once exceeded it returns 429 for *every* call for the next 5 minutes — not just the call that went over. A single token is shared by every managed resource, so adding resources anywhere raises the cost of every sweep.

A fresh provider pod sweeps all managed resources at once: measured at ~1186 calls in ~3 minutes for 131 resources, which is 99% of the quota in one burst. Steady state at `--poll=15m` is ~85 per 5 minutes. **So restarts are the risk, not steady running.**

If the budget panel is pegged, raise `--poll` in `provider-cloudflare-runtimeconfig.yaml`. **Do not set `--max-reconcile-rate`** — setting it to 2 silently stopped controllers reconciling entirely while DNS kept working and the provider still reported Healthy.

panels.title: Cloudflare API calls per 5m (quota 1200)
panels.description: upjet_resource_ext_api_duration_count is the provider's own counter of calls to the Cloudflare API. The 1200 line is the hard limit; crossing it 429s everything for 5 minutes.

panels.title: Budget used, last 5m
panels.description: Percent of the 1200-per-5-minute Cloudflare token quota currently consumed.

panels.title: Managed resources not syncing, by kind
panels.description: crossplane_managed_resource_{exists,synced} are per-GVK gauges, NOT per-resource — one series per installed CRD kind. `synced == 0` would match every kind that merely has no resources (241 of 242 here), so the difference against _exists is the real signal.

panels.title: External API call rate
panels.description: Zero while the provider pod is Running means controllers are not running at all — a failure mode that leaves the pod Ready and the Provider Healthy. Expect roughly 17 calls/min at --poll=15m with ~131 managed resources.

panels.title: Managed resources: exist vs synced vs ready
Provider restarts (each one costs a full-sweep burst)
panels.description: A restart re-observes every managed resource at once. That burst, not steady-state polling, is what exhausts the Cloudflare quota.
